The Palace of Cortés stands out in central Cuernavaca for its massive stone walls and fortress-like appearance. Its history is linked to Hernán Cortés and the early colonial era, while its central location makes it a convenient starting point for a walk through the city.

Today it houses the Regional Museum of the Peoples of Morelos. Its exhibits introduce the state's nature, culture, and people, revealing a regional history that stretches far beyond the name of the conquistador. The palace pairs well with a visit to the cathedral complex and a stroll along Cuernavaca's central streets.

## Palenque — the largest ruins of an ancient Maya city!

Palenque is the largest complex of ancient Maya city ruins, located in the northeast of the Mexican state of Chiapas. More than a thousand structures have been discovered here, covering a total area of 15 sq km, although only some have been thoroughly studied and restored. The modern town of Palenque lies a few kilometers east of the ruins. Translated from Spanish, Palenque means “wooden fence,” or a fortress, an enclosed place. Yet the town of Palenque in northern Chiapas was named almost 200 years before the famous ruins nearby were discovered in the eighteenth century.

This captivating part of Mexico invites you to explore its hidden archaeological treasures and gain a deeper understanding of them. While here, you will discover that the surroundings of Palenque offer breathtaking landscapes and mysteries of local life that are sure to inspire curiosity.

## Journey into the past!

The archaeological site of Palenque, one of the state's most important tourist attractions, lies just five miles from town. Situated on the first rise of the Tumbalá Mountains, it overlooks the floodplain of the Usumacinta River. On arrival, prepare to encounter the largest Mesoamerican stepped pyramid, the Temple of the Inscriptions, covered in hieroglyphs that have made a major contribution to the study of Maya civilization. The site is surrounded by beautiful natural areas, including the Misol-Ha waterfall and its large pool, where adventurous visitors may take a swim.

Begin exploring the neighborhood beside the lakes and trees of Tres de Febrero Park. The dome of the Galileo Galilei Planetarium appears between the treetops, and the paths along the water invite an unhurried stroll. Palermo reveals another side of the capital, where expansive green areas sit alongside dense city blocks.

The neighborhood is also home to the Botanical and Japanese Gardens, museums, and other places worth visiting separately. On a guided city itinerary, the stops depend on the particular excursion; a single visit to the district does not imply that every attraction is included.

Palermo is easy to combine with Recoleta and the historic neighborhoods of Buenos Aires. Together, these stops connect the architecture of the city center, everyday life on residential streets, and time to relax beside the water.
